name: Agentic Quality Engineering Platform
description: Enterprise multi-agent Quality Engineering platform where specialised AI agents collaborate across requirement analysis, test design, automation generation, execution, review, security and CI/CD.
problem: Modern engineering teams need quality workflows that span analysis, automation, execution and governance rather than isolated test scripts.
architecture: Multi-agent orchestration with specialised QE roles, shared context, evidence capture and human review checkpoints.
engineeringChallenge: Coordinating agent responsibilities while preserving traceability, governance and deterministic quality controls.
value: Demonstrates how AI can augment end-to-end Quality Engineering while keeping human oversight and measurable quality evidence in the loop.

name: Smart Test Designer
description: AI-powered test design platform combining Retrieval-Augmented Generation with enterprise test engineering workflows to generate contextual, traceable and reusable test scenarios.
problem: Test design often loses context across requirements, prior test assets and domain knowledge, causing duplication and inconsistent coverage.
architecture: RAG-based knowledge retrieval, configurable test generation, traceability, evaluation and multi-tenant workflow controls.
engineeringChallenge: Balancing retrieval quality, generation relevance, tenant isolation, traceability and practical enterprise workflow usability.
value: Shows how RAG and LLM evaluation can be applied to structured test design rather than generic text generation.
note: Portfolio case study; implementation repository is not linked publicly.

name: Playwright Enterprise Test Framework
description: Production-oriented Playwright automation framework designed for scalable enterprise UI and API testing with CI/CD integration and evidence-rich reporting.
problem: Teams need consistent, reusable automation foundations that scale beyond individual test suites.
architecture: Layered Playwright framework with page abstractions, API helpers, environment configuration, parallel execution, reporting and pipeline integration.
engineeringChallenge: Creating a framework that remains maintainable while supporting UI, API, retries, parallelism and deployment quality gates.
value: Provides a repeatable automation architecture that can be integrated into continuous delivery workflows.

name: AI Agent Evaluation Framework
description: Framework for evaluating AI agents across correctness, task completion, tool usage, reliability, hallucination risk, latency, cost and safety-oriented checks.
problem: AI agents can appear successful while using incorrect tools, producing unreliable reasoning paths or generating costly and unsafe outcomes.
architecture: Evaluation harness with task fixtures, tool-use validation, judge-based scoring, reliability metrics and evidence capture.
engineeringChallenge: Combining deterministic checks with model-based evaluation while keeping metrics explainable and repeatable.
value: Provides a structured approach for validating agent behaviour before AI-powered workflows are trusted in engineering processes.

name: RAG & LLM Evaluation Lab
description: Practical evaluation environment for measuring Retrieval-Augmented Generation quality across retrieval, context relevance, faithfulness and hallucination risk.
problem: RAG systems need measurable retrieval and answer-quality signals rather than subjective spot checks.
architecture: Evaluation pipeline spanning query sets, retrieval measurement, generation scoring, faithfulness checks and comparative experiments.
engineeringChallenge: Separating retrieval failures from generation failures and making evaluation results actionable.
value: Helps engineering teams reason about RAG quality using repeatable metrics and controlled experiments.

name: AI Test Failure Triage Agent
description: AI-powered agent for analysing test failures, logs, screenshots and execution evidence to classify probable causes and recommend remediation paths.
problem: Failure triage consumes engineering time and often requires manually correlating logs, screenshots and test history.
architecture: Evidence ingestion, failure classification, probable-cause analysis and remediation recommendation workflow.
engineeringChallenge: Producing useful triage guidance without overstating confidence or hiding the underlying evidence.
value: Demonstrates practical AI assistance for reducing repetitive failure-analysis effort while preserving engineer review.

name: Performance & Reliability Testing
description: Engineering toolkit demonstrating performance testing, reliability testing, service-level validation and observability-oriented quality practices.
problem: Functional correctness alone does not prove that a service will remain reliable under realistic load and operational conditions.
architecture: Workload models, service-level assertions, reporting and observability hooks organised around repeatable reliability checks.
engineeringChallenge: Designing tests that produce meaningful engineering signals rather than isolated load-test numbers.
value: Connects performance testing with reliability engineering and actionable service-quality evidence.

name: Test Data Engineering Toolkit
description: Reusable toolkit for generating, masking, provisioning and managing test data for automated testing environments.
problem: Automation becomes unreliable when test data is manually prepared, shared across suites or coupled to unstable environments.
architecture: Reusable data factories, masking/provisioning patterns and environment-aware test-data workflows.
engineeringChallenge: Keeping data realistic and reusable without exposing sensitive information or creating brittle dependencies.
value: Treats test data as an engineering capability that supports repeatable and secure automation.
